Messages.Author: cbo...@apdi.net
Messages.Body:
I recently moved to New Orleans and have found that while there are
alot of people who play cards games here, very few of those players
play V:tes. Because of this, I would like to hold a few demos here
and there to hopefully get more people interested in the game.
Unfortunately, I only know what the concept of a demo is (and a very
vague idea of how to run one). Is there anywhere on the net the
describes, or could any of you detail what goes on during a demo?

Also (LSJ, Ryan), I think it would be a really good idea if the (most
recent) Rulings, Clarifications and Erratta could be printed in an
issue of The Duelist. The reason being is that there was a situation
recently where I was in a game with some players (who do not have
access to the net) when one of them played a card illegally. I whipped
out my print out of the recent RC&E only to have them scoff at it
because they thought it was fake. In another game, I was lost to a
deck that abused Freak Drive and Majesty. They had never even heard
of NRA. If there are players who don't have net access, they don't have
any clue that there has been erratta and clarifications to many of the
cards. And if there is some officiality to the list, then those players
would have no choice but to abide by them. As it was, I lost several
games because of their unwillingness to recognize that those RC&E were
official. I do not imagine that my experience was an isolated incident.
I understand that there might? would? be some difficulty in getting it
printed in The Duelist due to their attitude towards the game, but I
think it is something that we should try to get done lest these RC&E
only be known (and recognized) by those of us who have net access.

Sorrow

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
cbo...@apdi.net wrote:
> Unfortunately, I only know what the concept of a demo is (and a very
> vague idea of how to run one). Is there anywhere on the net the
> describes, or could any of you detail what goes on during a demo?

I ran one here in Columbia, SC a few weeks before the tournament.
I built 14 decks. Each had 40 cards and a single-clan (camarilla)
crypt. And they were unfocused. Sure, the Brujah were focused on
combat and the Malks focused on bleeds - but not to the extent that
the deck would have a prayer in a tourney. I built all 14 out of
the 560 cards that Jennifer (WotC) scraped up from the storage units
at WotC - so the options were limited.

Anyway - the decks worked very well - lots of exposure to *all* the
rules (equipping, voting, retainers, combat, running out of cards,
stealth, intercept, etc.) in short order.

People showed up, and when four were available, I got them started
and waited for the next group of four.

Those without net access can write (paper, envelope, and stamp) for
a set of rulings and errata to the address printed in the rulebook.
Include a long SASE, with enough postage to cover mailing ten pages
or so back. Or, just request written confirmation that the rulings
on the net are official, and you ony need a regular SASE.

That should be official enough.

Messages.Author: Chris Shorb & Tammy Martin
Messages.Body:
cbo...@apdi.net wrote:

> Because of this, I would like to hold a few demos here
> and there to hopefully get more people interested in the game.

Good idea!

> Unfortunately, I only know what the concept of a demo is (and a very
> vague idea of how to run one). Is there anywhere on the net the
> describes, or could any of you detail what goes on during a demo?
>

First - find a good spot to play. If there are any local conventions,
this is good - you might get maximum exposure. Easier to find are your
local game store. Just tell them you need some space, and if they have some
Jyhad or Vampire, then they will have a good chance of selling more. Let
them know you will do the rest.
Make up some flyers with clear time and dates. Post them in the store
and anywhere else you think likely folk would congregate (outside Anne
Rice's house mayhaps?)

I have made up 61 card decks that are fairly themed and clan-based.
Each also has one each of the 15 of each vampire for each clan. I can
e-mail you the lists if you would like. The only thing that doesn't come
up, and I may need to change is that there is rarely any contestion, unless
you make up two of each deck and two folks grab the same clan deck. If you
don't have a lot of Jyhad commons, I could make and sell you as many as 4 of
each clan for $1.50 a piece plus shipping - the Wakes, Blood Dolls and
Hunting grounds cost about that much from Mark Korshavn.
The easiest way to teach the game to absolute newbies is to describe the
basis of the game - "You are an ancient vampire manipulating the strings
from afar. Your goal is to oust your prey." etc.
Describe the very basic terms, the very basic themes, the very basic
rules. Then give a brief outline of each clan, and how it tends to achieve
its ends - Malkavians are crazy, sneaky, and tend to bleed like mothers,
etc. Then let them pick the clan that appeals to them the most. Finally,
once they have picked the clans, play a game and teach as you go.
As an aside, I did not include Nosferatu in the mix because I felt that
they have the least clear course towards victory - they don't bleed, combat,
or vote as well as any of the other 6 basic clans, although they can be
really good combo decks. In short, I felt that Nosferatu-clan based decks
are too advanced for intro play - I could of course be totally wrong... : )

A few pointers -
1) bring lots of counters (35 per person you expect - pebbles, pennies,
toothpicks [the square kind, the round kind will roll away], etc.).
2) if you are playing, _don't win_ if you can help it. It looks bad
when the expert goes and trounces the newbies, you know?
3) take any opportunity to teach every and all things that happen in
the game, even if it might be stupid for you to do. Just the other day I
ran a demo, and one of the experienced players let his vamp go to torpor to
show how that happens. I know he wouldn't have done that in a tournament
situation.
4) if there are experienced players, do not let them turn the game into
the normal cutthroat Jyhad game - remember the demo is to teach new
players. Also - don't argue about rules, try to just let it flow...
5) if you can, give the decks away at the end of the demo.
6) be enthusiastic, patient, and have fun yourself - it is infectious.

Good Luck!

Chris
--
Chris Shorb & Tammy Martin
